title: ALMA Observations of the Debris Disk around the Young Solar Analog HD 107146
question: What is the radial distribution of mm-sized dust in the HD 107146 debris disk, and is there a gap or dip in the dust surface density?

data.angular_resolution: 1.15'' x 0.84'' (natural weighting, ~32 x 23 AU); 2.52'' x 2.25'' with 2'' taper

what.value: Millimeter flux densities at 0.88, 1.32 and 3.0 mm used for the spectral index

evidence.quote: By combining the flux densities measured for the HD 107146 debris disk at 0.88 mm, 1.25 mm, 1.32 mm and 3.0 mm by (cite: Hughes:2011), this work, (cite: Corder:2009) and (cite: Carpenter:2005), respectively

what.value: Dust absorption coefficients from porous-grain dust model

evidence.quote: The absorption coefficients $Q^{\rm{abs}}_\nu(a)$ were extracted from the dust models of (cite: Ricci:2010a)
$L^{\star}_{\nu}$ was derived from a black body with effective temperature $T = 5841$ K and bolometric luminosity $Log(L_\mathrm{bol}/L_\odot) = 0.04$ (cite: Carpenter:2008; Hillenbrand:2008)

recipe.goal: rescale visibility uncertainties and correct proper motion
recipe.method: Rescaled weights by median ratio of observed dispersion in uv cells to reported uncertainties; adjusted visibility phases for proper motion

recipe.goal: image continuum and measure integrated flux
recipe.method: clean imaging with natural and tapered weighting; flux integrated over area above 2σ in the tapered map

recipe.goal: derive grain size slope q from mm spectral index
recipe.method: Fit mm SED alpha, beta = alpha - 2, then Draine (2006) relation for q
assumptions: optically thin, Rayleigh-Jeans emission; rho = 1.2 g/cm3

recipe.method: Model image multiplied by Gaussian primary beam (24.3''), Fourier transformed and sampled at observed uv points; chi2 minimised for single power-law, power-law with gap, double power-law
key_parameters: model image 2048x2048 pixels of 0.015''; flux scaled as nu^(2+beta), beta=0.4
assumptions: axisymmetric, geometrically and optically thin disk; constant dust opacity across disk

recipe.method: F-test and Akaike information criterion between nested models

recipe.goal: CO upper limit and planet mass from gap width
recipe.method: LTE CO column/mass upper limit from non-detection; chaotic/crossing zone relation for planet mass using gap width
key_parameters: Tex = 50 K, FWHM 1.9 km/s, inclination ~20 deg

evidence.quote: The integrated flux density from the disk is 12.5 $\pm$ 1.3 mJy at 1.25 mm.
we measured a millimeter spectral index $\alpha = 2.42 \pm 0.16$
The $p$ value of $0.74^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$ indicates a surface density which is increasing with radius

answer_key.quantity: Delta chi2 gap vs single power-law

evidence.quote: which is lower by $\Delta\chi^2=43.0$ than the case of a single power-law model with no gap

answer_key.quantity: F-test statistic gap vs no gap

evidence.quote: The $F$-test statistics in this case has a value of $8 \times 10^{-10}$

answer_key.quantity: Planet mass from gap, crossing zone (coefficient 2.1)

not_stated_but_needed: Number of emcee walkers and iterations (only 'several hundreds') and burn-in
Priors and bounds on model parameters
Clean threshold, mask, cell and image size of the CLEAN images
Whether CASA clean or other tools were used for the visibility extraction and weight rescaling in detail
Which spectral windows/channels were used for continuum (line-free channels excluded CO)
Exact dust opacity table values and grain composition fractions
missing_for_reproduction: Exact clean parameters (mask, threshold, cell, image size)
Dust opacity table of Ricci et al. 2010a
score_reason: Public data and clear model equations, but MCMC settings, priors and imaging details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, explicit model parameterization, numeric results (gap radius/width, chi2).
